verdict.rationale: Keycloak is self-hosted on an operator-chosen database such as PostgreSQL, so the deployer controls where identity data lives. Admins can manage users and sessions through the admin console, Admin CLI and REST API, users can manage their own sessions, and tokens can be revoked through a revocation endpoint. However, nothing in the evidence explicitly documents deleting user data or setting retention policies. Missing for 10: documented user/account deletion (admin or self-service), configurable retention or expiration for events and logs, data-purge or export-for-deletion workflows, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
